Bryan Min

I'm a Ph.D. student at UC San Diego doing research in Human-Computer Interaction. I work with Prof. Haijun Xia as part of the Foundation Interface Lab.

My research centers on malleable software—interfaces that enable users to easily and expressively modify their software interface without code or a bloated list of settings.

Recently, I've been exploring malleable software under the world of generative user interfaces.

Generative UI is now building so many kinds of interfaces for us automatically. Traditional user interfaces show lists, widgets, text, images, and other forms of media. Now that generative UI is coming around, we're able to see that it can generate almost anything we envision. Yet, we're still generating the same traditional interfaces we've always had. Then, how do we design generative user interfaces that leverage the power of generative UI?

My research centers on malleable software—interfaces that enable users to easily, expressively, and broadly customize their software interface without code or a bloated list of settings. Specifically, I explore how we can bring malleable software to real-world, production-grade software systems, considering the tensions between designers, developers, and end-users. To do so, I study these three user groups, create interaction techniques, develop novel software systems, and create theoretical frameworks for bringing malleable software to more end-users.

My research centers on the question: How can we enable end users to easily customize their interfaces?

I'm interning at Microsoft Research right now, working with Nic Marquardt.
